stemMarkdown: A 60-litre solution contains 40% acid. How many litres of water must be added to dilute it to a 20% acid solution? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: The acid stays fixed at $24.00$ litres. For that to be $20\%$ of the solution, the total volume must become $\dfrac{24.00 \times 100}{20} = 120.00$ litres. Water to add $= 120.00 - 60 = 60.0$ litres.
altSolutionMarkdown: Only the solvent changes — anchoring on the unchanged solute is what makes these quick.
